title: Braiding Sweetgrass
author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
description: This book made me fall in love deeper with Earth, stat a bookclub, start this digital garden. Oh the gifts!

title: Mapa de Resistências em Portugal
author: BRAVA
description: A map of resistence movements in Portugal

title: The Faithful Gardener: A Wise Tale About That Which Can Never Die
author: Clarissa Pinkola Estés
description: I cried so much reading these beautiful stories

title: A máquina de fazer espanhóis
author: Valter Hugo Mãe
description: Sobbed and laughed really hard reading this. About getting old and all the complexities of the human experience

title: Anchored: How to Befriend Your Nervous System Using Polyvagal Theory
author: Deb Dana
description: Very eye opening, loved the exercises!

title: Siddhartha
author: Hermann Hesse
description: I read this book mostly through an insomnia and when I finished I felt the Om filling my body and I fell asleep. It is a balmy read, the images it portrays are useful and wise, the story perfectly imprinting lessons in your heart. Delicious

title: Active Hope: How to Face the Mess We're in without Going Crazy
author: Joanna Macy
description: It does what it sets out to do: teach you how to practice active hope. It is a wonderful tool for action.

title: All About Love: New Visions
author: bell hooks
description: “Love is as love does” I love the sense of agency through love that bell hooks provides, it’s refreshing. Love as action, love as craft, love as art, it gives us the autonomy to actually be loving agents

title: Research Is Ceremony: Indigenous Research Methods
author: Shawn Wilson
description: The way the book is structured and presents the indigenous research paradigm is much needed today for everybody. The notion that knowledge is collective and doesn’t belong to us is precious.

title: The Chalice and the Blade
author: Riane Eisler
description: Very thorough historical and anthropological account of partnership vs dominator societies, providing a solid framework to analyse today’s issues. I feel this book is so needed for us today to be able to reclaim our past, namely the gylanic partnership that did indeed exist, to be able to imagine new alternative futures.

title: Sacred Economics: Money, Gift, and Society in the Age of Transition
author: Charles Eisenstein
description: Very inspiring, challenging and necessary read. I am still lingering on all the new concepts this book has brought me, I might have to write an essay on it so I can integrate it better.

title: Sand Talk: How Indigenous Thinking Can Save the World
author: Tyson Yunkaporta

title: Food of the Gods: The Search for the Original Tree of Knowledge
author: Terence McKenna
description: I felt it was a bit rigid but definitely broadened my horizons

title: The More Beautiful World Our Hearts Know Is Possible (Sacred Activism)
author: Charles Eisenstein

title: Sowing Seeds in the Desert
author: Masanobu Fukuoka
description: Very hopeful, practical read, with such an inspiring example. I loved that he outs his philosophy at the core and applies it so beautifully

title: If Women Rose Rooted: The Power of the Celtic Woman
author: Sharon Blackie
description: Beautifully written, a Call in itself to plant our feet on the earth and rise up.

title: The Serviceberry: Abundance and Reciprocity in the Natural World
author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
description: Such a delicious read that prompts you into hopeful action.

title: The Secret Network of Nature
author: Peter Wohlleben
description: Soooo many interesting connections in nature and a lot of cool facts you can drop at dinner luring people into realising how cool nature is

title: Wawata - Moon Dreaming: Daily wisdom guided by Hina, the Māori moon
author: Hinemoa Elder
description: I bought this when I visited NZ, I loved learning about Māori moon wisdom

title: Anam Cara
author: John O'Donohue
description: I have read this a couple years ago and found it beautiful. It is this month's book for my book club!

title: Indigenous Religions & Ecology
author: Yale University
description: Good free course for introducing you to a vast range of indigenous cosmologies and their importance in ecology, with good resources to keep you exploring further

title: Learning for Sustainable Futures
author: University of Edinburgh
description: I thought for some reason this was gonna be really high tech but actually it so much about community, connection to place and love.

title: Repository of Future Methods
author: Futures Methods from Around the World
description: Research repository of future methods, including research on time, infrastructure, stewardship & ecology, community and agency. It's very fun to explore!
